To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the annual change in size, the annual change in market share, the annual change leverage, and the year effect are all significant drivers of restaurant firms' annual growth.

the annual change in size, market share, and leverage are significant drivers of annual growth for publicly listed restaurant firms in the US, whereas the annual change in book to market ratio, market risk premium and earnings growth do not have a significant relationship with annual growth.
annual changes in size and leverage are positively related to restaurant firms' one-year-ahead growth, while annual change in book-to-market is negatively related to growth.

the growth of the US restaurant industry is driven by a combination of factors.

the growth of the U. restaurant industry is driven by the following factors: (1) annual changes in size and share of market, (2) annual change in leverage, and (3) annual change in earnings growth, controlling for franchised operations, internationalization, year effects, and market risk premium.
